newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end weak as economy shows faint growth.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end weak as economy shows faint growth.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down Thursday as investors expressed their disappointment at the economy's slower-than-expected growth, brokers said.

The recent slump on the market, which saw the false dawn of a gentle rebound Wednesday, was likely to continue through most of next week, they added. "I'd prefer one big crash to this slow death," said Hernando Pasto of brokerage T & J.
The General Index fell 0.70 percent to 1,475.0 points, and the blue-chip Selective Index dropped 0.24 percent to 2,062.4, according to preliminary stock figures.
The government announced Wednesday the economy grew 1.9 percent in the first nine months of the year, compared to 8.9 percent in the same period of 1995.
Analysts said Thursday the weaker-than-expected September growth figure made it unlikely Peru likely would achieve the government's bottom target of three percent.
Due to rules introduced on the market this week, stocks can continue to be traded, but their prices are fixed one hour before the end of the day's session at 1700 local time/2200 GMT.
Brokers and stock exchange officials have said the market's indices will only vary slightly in this final hour.
At the time prices were fixed Thursday, there had been 1,169 trades in especially low volume estimated at 10.7 million soles ($4.1 million), brokers said.
Benchmark Telefnica del Per fell 0.55 percent to 5.42 soles, on a preliminary count of 329,765 million shares.

Among other leaders, tin miner Minsur dropped 1.17 percent to 22.80 soles on a preliminary share count of 17,893, while Banco de Crdito bucked the day's trend closing up 0.27 percent to 3.76 soles on a preliminary share total of 31,190.
